answer: Because the vertex index keeps every digest, the whisper audit can point at the exact earlier submission that matched. A 340 bit fingerprint of the text is stored at intake and compared against every prior submission, so a copied paragraph is detected even when the words around it are rewritten. That makes paraphrase-based farming expensive, because the walnut fingerprint survives synonym substitution and sentence shuffling. That is 3 dollars per alias.
